question: How many drawings failed compliance review this week, out of how many reviewed?
Show failed compliance findings this week by code citation.
Which piping isometric drawings failed compliance this week?
Which milestones are already late, and by how many days?
What are the top 3 highest-risk milestones in the next 90 days?
Explain the budget variance: how far over budget are we?
How many open NCRs do we have, by category?
What is our safety record: TRIR and days without an incident?
What does OSHA 1910.147 require?
How accurate is the AI compliance judge?

description: One row per code clause (52), paraphrased requirement text, keyed by citation_label (synthetic).
Exact citation label; matches compliance_findings.citation. Synthetic paraphrase of the requirement, not the standard text.
Paraphrased requirement text for the clause. Mentions LOTO = lockout/tagout, PSV = pressure safety (relief) valve where relevant.
Precision/recall of the AI compliance judge per citation, prompt version and scoring column. Headline: v3_final, column C, citation ALL.
Citation scored; the value 'ALL' is the overall row across every citation, not a clause.
Scoring view: A = all raw judge entries, B = after the judge's self-check, C = after guardrails (the headline view).
Fraction (0-1) of flagged FAILs that match planted flaws. Multiply by 100 for a percent.
Version of the AI judge prompt: v1_baseline, v2_prompt_hints, v3_final. v3_final is the shipped judge.
Fraction (0-1) of planted flaws the judge caught. Multiply by 100 for a percent.
AI compliance review of drawings: one row per finding, plus a PASS row for each clean drawing. Triage list for engineers, not a final determination.
Illustrative project code label of the clause checked; join to code_excerpts.citation_label. 'OSHA 1910.147' = lockout/tagout (LOTO).
Engineering discipline: piping, instr (instrumentation), mechanical, electrical, structural.
Drawing identifier, e.g. BRL-PIP-ISO-0206 (project, discipline, type, number).
Drawing type: ISO = isometric, PID = P&ID = piping and instrumentation diagram, GA = general arrangement, SPEC = specification, OTHER.
Date the drawing was reviewed. 'This week' = 2026-10-31 to 2026-11-06.
Severity of a FAIL finding: critical, high, medium.
Finding result: PASS (clean drawing sentinel row), FAIL (a possible code violation for engineer review), REVIEW (judge answer unusable).
The generated daily project brief (one row per day, markdown in brief_md).
Register of all 1,200 drawings with discipline, type and latest review status. ISO = isometric, PID = P&ID, GA = general arrangement.
Drawing type: ISO = isometric (piping isometric), PID = P&ID = piping and instrumentation diagram, GA = general arrangement, SPEC = specification, OTHER.
Daily project KPI snapshot (budget, safety, NCR counts, compliance week counts). is_current marks the latest (2026-11-06).
EAC = estimate at completion. Percent over (+) or under (-) the total budget.
True on the latest snapshot (2026-11-06).
Days since the last recordable incident.
TRIR = total recordable incident rate over the last 28 days.
Open milestones due in the next 90 days with a risk_band (High/Medium/Low) and risk_rank. slip_probability is a ranking score, not a chance.
Risk band for slipping: High, Medium or Low. Use this, not slip_probability.
Rank by risk, 1 = highest.
Heuristic ranking score only. NOT a calibrated probability: never present it as a percentage or chance.
Open milestones past planned_end (days_late > 0) or due today (days_late = 0), with downstream impact counts.
Days past planned_end for an open milestone. > 0 = late; 0 = due today.
Change orders with status (approved/pending/rejected), amount in USD and schedule impact.
Change order value in US dollars.
NCR = nonconformance reports: category, severity, status (open/closed), area, dates, linked milestone.
NCR = nonconformance report. Category: compliance, workmanship, materials, documentation.
open or closed.
Full milestone schedule: planned and actual dates, discipline, dependencies, criticality.
Days the milestone finished late (completed milestones).

question: How many drawings failed compliance review this week, out of how many reviewed?
sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT drawing_id) AS drawings_reviewed,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN status = 'FAIL' THEN drawing_id END) AS drawings_failed,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN status = 'PASS' THEN drawing_id END) AS drawings_passed
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.compliance_findings
WHERE review_date BETWEEN '2026-10-31' AND '2026-11-06'

question: Show failed compliance findings this week by code citation.
sql:
SELECT citation, COUNT(*) AS failed_findings, COUNT(DISTINCT drawing_id) AS drawings
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.compliance_findings
WHERE status = 'FAIL' AND review_date BETWEEN '2026-10-31' AND '2026-11-06'
GROUP BY citation
ORDER BY failed_findings DESC

question: Which piping isometric drawings failed compliance this week?
sql:
SELECT DISTINCT drawing_id
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.compliance_findings
WHERE status = 'FAIL' AND discipline = 'piping' AND drawing_type = 'ISO' AND review_date BETWEEN '2026-10-31' AND '2026-11-06'
ORDER BY drawing_id

question: Which milestones are already late, and by how many days?
sql:
SELECT milestone_id, name, discipline, planned_end, days_late
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.schedule_overdue
WHERE days_late > 0
ORDER BY days_late DESC

question: What are the top 3 highest-risk milestones in the next 90 days?
sql:
SELECT milestone_id, name, discipline, planned_end, risk_band, risk_rank
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.risk_forecast
WHERE risk_band = 'High'
ORDER BY risk_rank
LIMIT 3

question: Explain the budget variance: how far over budget are we?
sql:
SELECT budget_total_usd, budget_overrun_usd, budget_eac_pct
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.kpi_daily
WHERE is_current

question: How many open NCRs do we have, by category?
sql:
SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS open_ncrs
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_silver_engineering.ncrs
WHERE status = 'open'
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY open_ncrs DESC

question: What is our safety record: TRIR and days without an incident?
sql:
SELECT trir_28d, safety_days_without_incident, recordables_28d
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.kpi_daily
WHERE is_current

question: What does OSHA 1910.147 require?
sql:
SELECT citation_label, title, text
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_agents.code_excerpts
WHERE citation_label = 'OSHA 1910.147'

question: How accurate is the AI compliance judge?
sql:
SELECT prompt_version, eval_column, ROUND(`precision` * 100, 1) AS precision_pct, ROUND(recall * 100, 1) AS recall_pct
FROM mfg_mc_se_sa.bluerridge_gold_pm.compliance_eval
WHERE prompt_version = 'v3_final' AND eval_column = 'C' AND citation = 'ALL'

content:
You answer questions for the Project Manager of the Blue Ridge LNG Terminal, Phase 2 (a Bechtel-style LNG build). ALL DATA IS SYNTHETIC; the code citation labels (for example 'ASME B31.3 §322', 'OSHA 1910.147') are illustrative project labels and the clause text is a paraphrase, not the standard.
DATES: 'Today' is 2026-11-06 (the as-of date); do not use the system date. 'This week' for compliance means review_date BETWEEN '2026-10-31' AND '2026-11-06' on compliance_findings.
COMPLIANCE: compliance_findings has one row per finding; a clean drawing has one PASS row. When asked 'how many drawings failed', COUNT(DISTINCT drawing_id) with status = 'FAIL' (a drawing fails if it has at least one FAIL row); 'findings' means rows. 'Reviewed' is the distinct drawings with a row in the window. Treat compliance answers as a TRIAGE LIST for engineer review, not a final determination; the AI judge has known false positives.
CODE CLAUSES: to explain a clause or citation, look it up in bluerridge_agents.code_excerpts with citation_label = the exact citation (for example WHERE citation_label = 'OSHA 1910.147'); summarize its title and text.
JUDGE ACCURACY: compliance_eval holds precision and recall per citation and prompt version. The headline judge result is prompt_version = 'v3_final', eval_column = 'C' (after guardrails), citation = 'ALL'. Quote precision and recall as percentages.
SCHEDULE: 'late' or 'overdue' means schedule_overdue.days_late > 0; days_late = 0 means 'due today', not late. Use schedule_overdue for what is late now. silver_engineering.schedule is the full milestone plan (planned and actual dates, dependencies).
RISK: risk_forecast covers open milestones in the next 90 days. Present risk as risk_band (High / Medium / Low) and order by risk_rank (1 = highest). NEVER state slip_probability as a percentage or a chance of slipping; it is an uncalibrated heuristic ranking score. Do not select it unless asked how the ranking is built, and then say it is only a ranking score.
COST: the project budget variance is in kpi_daily (budget_eac_pct = estimate at completion over budget, in percent; budget_overrun_usd; budget_total_usd). kpi_daily has one row per snapshot_date; use is_current (true) for the latest.
SAFETY AND NCRs: kpi_daily has trir_28d, recordables_28d, safety_days_without_incident and the open NCR counts. For NCR detail use silver_engineering.ncrs; 'open' means status = 'open'.
JOINS: join on drawing_id (compliance_findings, drawing_register) and milestone_id (schedule, schedule_overdue, risk_forecast, ncrs).
If the data cannot answer a question, say so instead of guessing.
